what_worked: Exceptional narrative arc from power law through categories, distribution, and marketplace with honest limitations slide.
fix_next: Several median figures (Education $2,142 vs $2,435; AI $446 vs $503; top-10 share 81.8% vs 49.6%) diverge materially from reference data—audit denominators.
verdict: Strong, well-structured data story undermined by multiple numeric inaccuracies.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: Top-10 share claimed 81.8% vs reference 49.6%—likely using MRR not 30-day revenue, but the subtitle says 'earn more than the other 990 combined' which is false at 49.6%. Slide 6: Education median $2,142 vs reference $2,435; AI median $446 vs $503; Marketing $1,586 vs $2,369.50—systematic understatement, possibly using MRR instead of 30-day revenue or different filters. Slide 8: Stripe share stated 64.4% / $11.8M MRR vs reference 636 companies (63.6%) and $13.5M revenue—minor but the revenue figure is notably lower. Slide 1: '$133.8M revenue last 12 months' and '500,597 active subscriptions' are unverifiable against reference but plausible aggregates.

evidence.insight: Slide 5 growth-by-band analysis and slide 10 revenue-multiple-by-price-band go well beyond chart description; slide 6 'crowded not richest' reframes AI narrative meaningfully; slide 8 domain-rating vs social following comparison is genuinely useful.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis ('who is making money') established on slide 1, developed through power law → distribution → categories → B2B/B2C → distribution channels → geography → marketplace → limitations → synthesis. Each finding builds on the prior. Slide 12 synthesizes five conclusions that map back to specific findings.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 explains dataset structure, coverage rates, and field categories before any analysis. Slide 11 dedicates an entire page to four limitations (survivorship, sparse traffic, anonymous entries, single window). Coverage footnotes on every analytical slide with sample sizes.
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 revenue share is the most consequential error: 81.8% (slide 3) vs 49.6% reference—this is the slide's headline claim. Category medians systematically differ from reference (Education off by ~$293, Marketing off by ~$784, AI off by ~$57). The deck appears to use MRR throughout rather than 30-day revenue, which is a defensible choice but creates discrepancies when the reference uses 30-day revenue. Zero-revenue count 197 (slide 4) vs reference 216 for 30-day revenue suggests MRR-based counting.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/coral palette throughout. Good use of log scale on slide 8. Bar charts are clean with direct labels. Side panels with callout stats complement charts without cluttering. Slide density is well-managed—no slide feels overloaded or empty. Chart types are appropriate (horizontal bars for categories, grouped bars for distribution comparison).
evidence.ai_slop: none—the deck avoids generic filler, consulting language, and decorative graphics. Every element serves the analysis.
